dedupe_keys.name: opentraj benchmark collection of human trajectory datasets

description: OpenTraj gathers publicly available datasets for human trajectory prediction and provides tools to load, visualise and analyse them, accompanying the paper 'OpenTraj: Assessing Prediction Complexity in Human Trajectories Datasets' by Amirian and co-authors. Its table lists 25 datasets with scene descriptions, trajectory counts, coordinate systems and frame rates, including ETH, UCY, the Stanford Drone Dataset, Grand Central station, Jülich's HERMES experiments, inD, Edinburgh Informatics Forum, Oxford Town Centre, DUT and CITR vehicle-crowd interaction, VRU, nuScenes and Waymo. The toolkit has loaders that put trajectories into pandas data frames, benchmark indicator scripts and a simple playback viewer. Coverage: street, campus, station and intersection scenes in Europe, North America and Asia. Access: the repository links to each dataset's own site or download. Licence: none stated for the repository; the source datasets' terms apply. Caveats: coordinate systems and frame rates differ, some sets are image-only, and several links point to older hosts. Simulation uses: calibrating and benchmarking pedestrian movement and crowd models for public spaces. Related records: the Jülich pedestrian dynamics archive.
